To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) a federated database management approach is the appropriate solution to the problem of data integration in a manufacturing environment where organizations cooperate as well the compete; (2) complete transparency, assumed mandatory in distributed database management systems, is neither feasible nor desirable; and (3) a universal relation approach to the design of the federated database system is appropriate.

(1) a universal relation approach to the FDBS is a feasible alternative to the integration approach, (2) the universal relation approach is based on schema coordinatation and not schema integration, and (3) the universal relation is an abstraction that is useful to the FDBA and to the user.

a federated approach is appropriate in a manufacturing environment that involves multiple, autonomous, and heterogeneous organizations; that a universal relation model is an appropriate model for the FDB system in this environment; and that the query processing paradigm is based on query transformations and heterogeneity resolution.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a federated database management system that is appropriate to a manufacturing environment.
the design of FDBSs for a new class of applications, namely, those involving multiple cooperating organizations.

the design of a FDBS that supports a manufacturing environment where organizations cooperate as well a compete with one another, and where each organization is free to change data structure and semantics of its component databases.

a federated metadata model can be used to achieve the desired level of interoperability among cooperating databases in a manufacturing environment without sacrificing the autonomy of the individual databases.
